thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: PagerDuty incident fired for service=prod-inference (severity=page) — high tail latency observed. PD link: https://pd.example/INCIDENT/PD12345

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident PD12345 assigned to alex-sre — urgent.

alex-sre: ack'd on-call. I'm looking. Initial glance: spike in p50->p99 for /v1/generate starting ~11:12 UTC.

priya-sre: on it as backup. I'm pulling tail logs from the realtime router.

megan-support: saw 3 customer tickets about slow responses — corp-customer A and startup-B reporting timeouts. I'll start triage notes.

emily-pm: tagging for visibility — potential customer impact. Keep me posted with scope.

alex-sre: quick findings: upstream queuing on router pod set-2, CPU on that node at ~95%. KV cache miss rate jumped.

josh-eng: could be a bad batch of long prompts causing KV pressure. Any correlated deploys?

priya-sre: checking deploy history... none in last 6h. Rolling 10m metrics: model-large instances saw memory pressure + GC spikes.

ryan-ops: autoscaler didn't trigger because we've hit max reserved GPUs in the pool. Requesting burst capacity now.

incident-bot: ACTIONS: 1) alex-sre to own mitigation. 2) priya-sre gather logs + scale commands. 3) megan-support update customers. 4) josh-eng standby for rollback.

alex-sre: mitigation plan: (a) divert 30% traffic to fallback model-small-v2, (b) enable burst pool (if approved), (c) restart router pods on node-2. Doing (a) now.

josh-eng: +1 for diverting traffic. Quick config snippet to change routing weight:
```
route-config set-weight --route inference-prod --model small-v2 --weight 0.3
```

priya-sre: applied routing change, verifying. Cache pressure easing on small-v2; p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 0.9s for diverted requests.

megan-support: posted initial note to affected customers: "We're investigating increased inference latency — temporary mitigation in progress (diverting to fallback model). We'll update within 15 minutes."

alex-sre: requesting burst pool enable via ops console. ryan-ops, can you approve?

ryan-ops: approving now, enabling +2 GPUs to dedicated pool. ETA 90s for capacity to be recognized.

incident-bot: system note: burst capacity change accepted by ops. New capacity visible in 38s.

priya-sre: restarting router pods on node-2 to clear possible stuck requests. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/router -n prod --selector=zone=node-2`

josh-eng: monitoring logs — I see repeated slow kv-fetches for prefix hashes starting with 0x7b4a. Might be a bad prompt batch from customer X.

megan-support: customer X confirmed they sent a bulk job ~11:10 UTC (long prompt stream). Asking them to pause if possible.

emily-pm: prioritize minimising customer impact. If customer X is non-critical, throttling them temporarily is OK. Otherwise inform them first.

alex-sre: throttled customer X rate by 70% as of 11:25 UTC. That dropped overall queue depth by ~45%.

priya-sre: with routing + throttle + burst, overall p99 across clusters is down to ~1.1s. Some tail still elevated on eu-cluster-1.

ryan-ops: eu cluster autoscaler showing ephemeral pod failures — pulling node kernel logs. There was an OOM on model-worker-3 at 11:16 UTC. Investigating node-level oom.

incident-bot: please confirm customer impact severity: megan-support?

megan-support: customer impact: intermittent timeouts and slow responses for ~12 paying customers, several support tickets open. No data loss. Severity = high for affected customers. I'll sync with account teams.

alex-sre: current status: mitigation successful for majority, p99 under 1.2s for us-east, eu still ~1.9s. I'm going to run a config to bias more requests away from eu until ops resolves node oom.

josh-eng: quick mitigation to bias traffic: `route-config set-region-weight --region eu-west-1 --weight 0.6` (reduce eu weight).

priya-sre: applied region weight change. eu p99 trending down. Node remediation: ryan-ops is evicting oom'd worker and draining node for inspection.

ryan-ops: node drained, replaced kernel module, redeployed worker with adjusted ulimits. Monitoring.

megan-support: posted update to customers: "Mitigation in place; performance improving. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA for full recovery."

emily-pm: good. Please capture timeline and impact for post-incident report. Prioritize root cause: KV cache misses + long customer batch + autoscale limits + node OOM.

alex-sre: agreeing — next steps: 1) full heap/profile from oom'd worker, 2) add soft-limits to customer bulk jobs (rate-limiter), 3) improve autoscaler alert threshold to preempt async queuing.

josh-eng: I'll own rate-limiter change. Quick patch: enforce max prompt tokens per minute per API key and a sliding window. Rollout to canary in 15m.

priya-sre: collecting logs and saving artifacts. Uploading to /incidents/PD12345/artifacts.tar.gz

incident-bot: NOTE: alex-sre is the current incident owner. If ownership changes, please state explicitly.

alex-sre: handoff plan: I'm going offline at 12:30 UTC. priya-sre will take lead after that. If anything spikes beyond p99>2.5s or error rate >1% notify PD and page priya.

priya-sre: acknowledged — I'll take over at 12:30 UTC. I'll set a 5-minute status ping.

megan-support: continuing customer comms; will escalate accounts where SLO breach risk.

ryan-ops: creating follow-up ticket to review autoscaler limits and burst pool policy. Ticket INF-4567.

alex-sre: current summary for interim report: Root cause likely combination of big prompt batch from customer X causing KV cache churn + node-level OOM + autoscaler at max capacity. Mitigations: traffic diversion, throttling offending key, enabling burst capacity, node replacement. Service partially restored; monitoring stable.

emily-pm: thanks. Capture impact numbers: number of affected requests, customers, minutes degraded. We'll include in the postmortem.

priya-sre: status ping (11:45 UTC): metrics stable, no new timeouts reported in last 5m.

megan-support: update posted to all affected customers and account teams.

alex-sre: handing off to priya-sre at 12:30 UTC as planned. Priya — full incident runbook and links in thread.

priya-sre: taking ownership now (12:30 UTC). Will run through checklist and confirm when we can move to monitoring-only and close.

incident-bot: Reminder: create postmortem at /pm/PD12345 within 24h and tag eng/runtime, eng-sre, support.

priya-sre: will draft postmortem. Closing notes: no customer data exposure, no failed model responses. Estimated total customer-visible downtime window: ~18 minutes (11:12–11:30 UTC) for peak degradation.

megan-support: that's the timeline I'll reference with accounts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ryan-ops: marking node issue as mitigated. Follow-ups created for kernel anomaly and autoscale thresholds.

alex-sre: thanks team — leaving notes and escalation checklist for priya.

priya-sre: logging final checks. If stable for next 30m we'll close the incident.

megan-support: closing customer comms loop at 13:00 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident PD12345 status: monitoring. Owner=priya-sre.

priya-sre: final ping at 13:28 UTC — stable for 58 minutes. Closing incident to monitoring-only. Will publish postmortem draft in ~2 hours.

megan-support: confirmed with accounts. No further tickets.

alex-sre: thanks everyone, good job moving fast and coordinating the handoff.

josh-eng: nice work.

ryan-ops: good job.

(megan-support, alex-sre, priya-sre, josh-eng, ryan-ops, emily-pm listed above are participants)
